> **When a TGV is late, who is to blame: the trains, the tracks, or the passengers?**

The original project is an interactive **Bokeh server app** that works as the
slide deck of our talk: a hook, a map of the rail network, then four acts that
follow Shneiderman's mantra, *overview first, zoom and filter, then details on
demand* [@shneiderman1996eyes]. This chapter tells the same story for the
portfolio. The figures below are **re-drawn in R** from the same SNCF files,
downloaded by code at render time, so every number in the text is recomputed
rather than copied from the report.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
                  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  legend.position = "top"))

accent <- "#D55E00"   # vermillion: the series the story follows
context <- "grey65"   # everything else
```
:::


## Data

SNCF publishes three monthly punctuality files on data.gouv.fr. Each level of
the story uses **its own file**: the national rate is not the average of axes
or routes, because one train can belong to several routes but counts only once
nationally.

| File | Level | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `reglarite-mensuelle-tgv-nationale` | all TGVs, monthly, from 2015 | Act 1: the big picture |
| `regularite-mensuelle-tgv-axes` | per axis (Nord, Est, Atlantique, Sud-Est, Europe, OUIGO) | Act 2: regions |
| `regularite-mensuelle-tgv-aqst` | per route, with train counts and six delay causes, from 2018 | Acts 3 and 4 |


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sncf_url <- "https://ressources.data.sncf.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/%s/exports/csv?use_labels=true"
tgv_files <- c(national = "reglarite-mensuelle-tgv-nationale",   # (sic: SNCF's file name)
               axes     = "regularite-mensuelle-tgv-axes",
               routes   = "regularite-mensuelle-tgv-aqst")

dir.create(here("data", "raw"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
tgv_path <- \(key) here("data", "raw", paste0(tgv_files[[key]], ".csv"))
for (key in names(tgv_files)) {
  if (!file.exists(tgv_path(key)))
    download.file(sprintf(sncf_url, tgv_files[[key]]), tgv_path(key), mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
}

read_sncf <- \(key) read_delim(tgv_path(key), delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE)
```
:::


### Cleaning decisions

The full log of ambiguities and decisions lives in the project's
`DATA_NOTES.md`. The ones that matter for this chapter:

- **% late is computed from counts**: late trains ÷ (planned − cancelled).
  Yearly and group figures **sum the counts first, then divide**, never
  averaging percentages.
- **Months with zero planned trains are dropped** (nothing to measure).
- **Rows whose six cause shares are all zero** keep their counts but are left
  out of the cause analysis.
- **Cause shares are weighted** by each row's number of late trains, so a
  3-train route does not weigh as much as a 300-train one.
- **Causes are compared on full years 2018–2025**: the categories appear to
  change around May 2026.
- The national file has no counts, so its yearly rate is the **mean of monthly
  percentages**, an approximation we state as such.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
national <- read_sncf("national") |>
  transmute(date = ym(Date), pct_late = 100 - `Régularité composite`)

axes <- read_sncf("axes") |>
  transmute(date = ym(Date), axis = Axe, pct_late = 100 - `Régularité composite`)

foreign <- c("BARCELONA", "MADRID", "FRANCFORT", "STUTTGART",
             "ZURICH", "LAUSANNE", "GENEVE", "ITALIE")

routes <- read_sncf("routes") |>
  transmute(
    date = ym(Date), service = Service,
    departure = `Gare de départ`, arrival = `Gare d'arrivée`,
    planned = `Nombre de circulations prévues`,
    cancelled = `Nombre de trains annulés`,
    late = `Nombre de trains en retard à l'arrivée`,
    External = `Prct retard pour causes externes`,
    Infrastructure = `Prct retard pour cause infrastructure`,
    `Traffic management` = `Prct retard pour cause gestion trafic`,
    `Rolling stock` = `Prct retard pour cause matériel roulant`,
    `Station management` = `Prct retard pour cause gestion en gare et réutilisation de matériel`,
    Passengers = `Prct retard pour cause prise en compte voyageurs (affluence, gestions PSH, correspondances)`
  ) |>
  filter(planned > 0) |>
  mutate(
    ran  = planned - cancelled,
    year = year(date),
    type = case_when(
      departure %in% foreign | arrival %in% foreign ~ "International",
      str_starts(departure, "PARIS") | str_starts(arrival, "PARIS") ~ "To/from Paris",
      TRUE ~ "Province to province"
    )
  )

national_yearly <- national |>
  group_by(year = year(date)) |>
  summarise(pct_late = mean(pct_late), months = n(), .groups = "drop")

latest      <- national_yearly |> slice_max(year)
last_month  <- max(national$date)
worst_prev  <- national_yearly |> filter(year < latest$year) |> slice_max(pct_late)
```
:::


## The hook: about one TGV in six

::: {.stat-row}
::: {.stat}
[16.7 %]{.value}
[of TGVs late in 2026 (Jan–Sep)]{.label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[2026]{.value}
[the worst year since 2015]{.label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[3,423,034]{.value}
[route-trains analysed since 2018]{.label}
:::
:::

## Act 1 · The big picture


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
events <- tribble(
  ~start,       ~end,         ~label,
  "2018-04-01", "2018-06-30", "Rail strike",
  "2019-12-01", "2020-01-31", "Pension strike",
  "2020-03-15", "2020-05-15", "COVID lockdown",
  "2022-07-01", "2022-07-31", "Heatwave",
  "2023-01-15", "2023-04-15", "Pension strikes"
) |> mutate(across(c(start, end), as.Date))

ggplot(national, aes(date, pct_late)) +
  geom_rect(data = events, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#1D3557", alpha = .08) +
  geom_text(data = events, aes(x = start, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            angle = 90, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.4, size = 2.8, colour = "#1D3557") +
  geom_line(colour = context) +
  geom_line(data = filter(national, year(date) == latest$year), colour = accent, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Trains late")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of TGVs arriving late each month since 2015. Shaded bands mark major events (from news sources, not from the data): they coincide with peaks but do not prove a cause.](02-tgv-delays_files/figure-html/fig-tgv-national-1.png){#fig-tgv-national width=672}
:::
:::




Punctuality is getting worse: 2026 is the worst year in the data
(@fig-tgv-national). The COVID years were the most punctual
(9.2 % and
9.4 % late in 2020 and 2021), but
the month-to-month number of trains barely relates to the share late, so
"fewer trains" is not a supported explanation. Summers are worst:
**July** averages 14.8 %
late against 9.4 % in
March.

## Act 2 · Not all of France is equal


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
regional <- c("Est", "Atlantique", "Nord", "Sud-Est")
axes_yearly <- axes |>
  group_by(axis, year = year(date)) |>
  summarise(pct_late = mean(pct_late), months = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(months == 12)

axes_yearly |>
  filter(axis %in% regional) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, pct_late, colour = axis)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(national_yearly, months == 12), aes(year, pct_late),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 1.6, alpha = .5) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Est = accent, Atlantique = "#0072B2",
                                 Nord = "#009E73", `Sud-Est` = "#56B4E9")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Trains late", colour = NULL)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Yearly share of late TGVs on the four regional axes, with the national rate in grey. Only years with twelve months of data are shown.](02-tgv-delays_files/figure-html/fig-tgv-axes-1.png){#fig-tgv-axes width=672}
:::
:::




The axes diverge over time (@fig-tgv-axes). **Est** was the most punctual
regional axis every year until 2022, after which the ranking shuffles.
Across all six axes, the **Europe** (international) axis has been the worst in
3 of the
4 full years since 2022.

## Act 3 · It's where, not how far



In the app, a route map and a duration-versus-delay scatter share one data
source, so selecting routes on either highlights them on both. The first
hypothesis, *long routes are late more often*, did not hold: trip duration
barely relates to the share late. What does matter is **where** a route runs.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
routes |>
  group_by(year, type) |>
  summarise(pct_late = 100 * sum(late) / sum(ran), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(year, pct_late, colour = type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Province to province` = accent,
                                 `To/from Paris` = "#0072B2",
                                 International = context)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty_breaks()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Trains late", colour = NULL)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Yearly share of late trains by type of route (counts summed, then divided). International routes rest on far fewer trains.](02-tgv-delays_files/figure-html/fig-tgv-types-1.png){#fig-tgv-types width=672}
:::
:::


Routes between two regional cities that do not go through Paris are late more
often (19.6 %) than routes to or from
Paris (13.9 %), and the gap holds in
**every year** from 2018 to 2025, by
2.7 to
8.7 points (@fig-tgv-types). The data
shows *where* delays concentrate, not *why*.

## Act 4 · Who's to blame?


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cause_cols <- c("External", "Infrastructure", "Traffic management",
                "Rolling stock", "Station management", "Passengers")
groups <- c(External = "External", Infrastructure = "Tracks",
            `Traffic management` = "Tracks", `Rolling stock` = "Trains",
            `Station management` = "Trains", Passengers = "Passengers")

causes <- routes |>
  filter(year %in% 2018:2025, rowSums(across(all_of(cause_cols))) > 0) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(cause_cols), names_to = "cause", values_to = "share") |>
  mutate(group = factor(groups[cause], levels = c("Tracks", "Trains", "External", "Passengers")),
         late_trains = share / 100 * late)

cause_total <- causes |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(n = sum(late_trains), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))
pct_of <- \(g) number(cause_total$pct[cause_total$group == g], accuracy = 1)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
causes |>
  group_by(year, group) |>
  summarise(n = sum(late_trains), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), pct, fill = fct_rev(group))) +
  geom_col(width = .75, colour = "white", linewidth = .4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Tracks = "#D55E00", Trains = "#0072B2",
                               External = "#009E73", Passengers = "#CC79A7"),
                    breaks = c("Tracks", "Trains", "External", "Passengers")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of late trains", fill = NULL)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Delay causes as attributed by SNCF, weighted by the number of late trains (2018–2025). Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe palette.](02-tgv-delays_files/figure-html/fig-tgv-causes-1.png){#fig-tgv-causes width=672}
:::
:::


Mostly the tracks (@fig-tgv-causes). Weighted by late trains, **tracks**
(infrastructure + traffic management) account for 44 % of
delays, **trains** (rolling stock + station management) 27 %,
**external** causes 21 % and **passengers**
8 %. Two caveats: SNCF attributes the causes itself, and
the "tracks first" result depends on our grouping, since no single SNCF
category dominates on its own.

## Visualisation and accessibility choices

- **One accent colour per chart**: grey for context, vermillion for the series
  the story follows.
- **Act 3 colour scales are fixed** at 0–30 % late (ColorBrewer YlOrRd), so a
  colour means the same thing whatever year is selected.
- **Two accessibility approaches**: the cause chart does not rely on colour
  alone (Okabe-Ito palette checked with a colour-vision-deficiency simulator,
  white gaps, legend and optional hatch patterns); the punctuality chart has
  text alternatives (a written summary generated from the data, detailed
  tooltips and a drawer with the full data table).
- **Iterated on feedback**: after a review with the teacher, the six axis
  panels became one comparable chart, the route-type dropdown became a
  carousel of cards, and the map colour scale moved from a single red hue to a
  sequential yellow-to-red scale.

## Limitations

- Monthly totals, not individual trains.
- Delay causes are self-reported by SNCF; the categories seem to change in
  2026 and the passenger share jumps suddenly in January 2021.
- The national and route-level rates differ in level (for example
  13.4 %
  vs 15.1 %
  in 2025) for reasons we could not confirm, so they are never compared
  directly.
- Correlation is not causation: the charts show where and when delays happen,
  not why.

## Running the original app

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chaudharymfaizan78/TGV-delays-DataViz.git
cd TGV-delays-DataViz
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
bokeh serve --show Bokeh_App
```
